issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int number and a String reason), but the solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. The template does not provide a method signature (only a TODO), so students following the problem/UML would implement a two-parameter method, while the solution demonstrates a different single-parameter signature. This inconsistency can confuse students about the required method signature and expected parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by changing the solution method to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update its body to add the new guest students (and optionally record or log the reason). Alternatively, if the intended design is a single-parameter method, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) to remove the second parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an integer number of new guest students plus a String reason), but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single integer parameter. This discrepancy in the method signature creates a mismatch between the stated requirement and the provided implementation, causing students to be unable to directly map the required API (including the reason parameter) to the solution/template.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem statement by changing the solution (and template) method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and, if appropriate, store or log the reason. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) if the reason parameter is intentionally omitted.
